sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of High-Power Fiber Laser Metal Sheet Cutting Systems

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified system; unitary national corporate-law regime without sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty of 14 November 2005 (in force 1 July 2008; replaces the 1992 BIT)
China–Spain Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 22 November 1990 (entered into force 25 May 1991; effective 1 January 1992), as amended by the Protocol of 13 February 1992
Spain–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 22 February 1990 (in force 30 November 1990) — relevant for US-based shareholders
Spain–Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty of 10 October 2006 (in force 2008) — LATAM bridge strategy
Spain–Chile Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 2 April 2003 (in force 2004) — LATAM bridge strategy
EU–Mercosur Association Agreement (concluded at political level in December 2025, pending signature and ratification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April 2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 and subsequent amendments); Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May 2014 approving the Regulation implementing Law 10/2010; Law 11/2018 of 28 December 2018 and Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 transposing EU beneficial-ownership rules; Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July 2010), Articles 13–14; Mercantile Registry Regulation (Royal Decree 1784/1996), Articles 51–56; UBO Declaration Form (Formulario de Titularidad Real) filed with the Registro Mercantil at incorporation and updated annually; SEPBLAC guidelines and EBA AML/CFT risk-factor guidance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted access following CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022, joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20: Spanish UBO data accessible to competent authorities — SEPBLAC, AEAT, CNMV, judicial bodies — and to AML obliged entities performing statutory customer due diligence; no general public access; nominee vehicles must fully disclose beneficial ownership or face registration refusal and fines; all SL shareholders and UBOs reconfirmed via the Libro Registro de Socios and annual UBO declaration)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each foreign individual shareholder's passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's home country (upstream) / Spanish notary for verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention of 1961 (if home state is a Contracting Party, including China since 7 November 2023) OR Consular Legalization through the Spanish Embassy/Consulate for non-Hague states; followed by sworn translation by a Spanish Traductor Jurado

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder General para la constitución de la sociedad) granted by foreign individual or corporate shareholders in favor of the Spanish incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the home jurisdiction, entered in the public protocol
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; Spanish sworn translation required; the instrument must expressly list powers for SL incorporation, bank account opening, and tax filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Vigencia) or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies house, corporate registry, or chamber of commerce of the shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; must be issued within 90 days before presentation to the Spanish notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholders' resolution of any corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada and appointing its signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign shareholder, attested to by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) assignment certificate for each foreign individual shareholder or director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General de la Policía (Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras, Spain) or Spanish Consulate in the home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Spanish public document — no apostille required; original assignment certificate or valid NIE identification must be exhibited to the notary and the corporate bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory (i) identity verification under Law 10/2010 Articles 3–5; (ii) enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under Articles 14–15 and RD 304/2014 Article 24, including beneficial-ownership reasoning and source-of-funds evidence; (iii) screening against the UN Consolidated List, EU Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and 2580/2001 lists, EU autonomous sanctions, Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, OFAC SDN List, and national judicial entries; (iv) automated red-flag triggers for non-resident corporate owners, low-tax jurisdictions, and nominee arrangements; (v) 10-year record-keeping obligation under Law 10/2010 Article 25; (vi) reporting of suspicious transactions to SEPBLAC through the official e-portal. The ISIC 2819 high-power fiber laser manufacturing scope is classified as AML tier Low_Risk_Standard, therefore standard customer due diligence applies; the designated payment rails (SWIFT Letter of Credit and TT wire transfer) are compliant instruments and do not trigger additional licensing requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) — online application through the Colegio de Registradores electronic platform at www.registradores.org (e-service 'Certificado de Denominación Social'); physical service at its Madrid office; negative name certificate (certificado negativo de denominación) typically issued within 24–72 hours, or same-day on expedited application.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Royal Decree 1784/1996 Articles 402–414, the proposed SL name must be written in Spanish, in any of Spain's co-official languages (Catalan, Galician, Basque), or in any European Union official language using Roman characters; non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet; accented vowels and 'ñ' are permitted; the denomination must not be identical or phonetically/visually similar to an existing registered name; purely generic descriptions and names contradicting law, morality, or public order are refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Spain, Nacional, Oficial (require prior authorization of the Consejo de Ministros)
Gobierno, Estado, Ministerio, Administración, Ayuntamiento, Comunidad, Diputación
Banco, Banco de España, Caja de Ahorros, Seguro, Mutualidad, Fondo de Garantía (require prior Bank of Spain or Directorate-General of Insurance authorization)
Cruz Roja, Policía, Guardia Civil, Fuerzas Armadas, Aduana
Federación, Gremio, Cámara, Colegio, Asociación (when the actual legal form of the entity does not correspond to the term used)
Universidad, Colegio Mayor, Fundación, Obra Social
Bolsa, IBEX, Unión Europea, OTAN, and international organization names or emblems
Third-party registered trademarks (e.g., TRUMPF, BOSCH, IPG) reproduced without license
Names identical, phonetically equivalent, or visually confusing with a denomination already recorded in the Central Mercantile Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate reserves the denomination for 3 (three) months from the date of issuance; no extension is available, but a fresh application with a new priority date may be filed after expiry. On rejection: (1) read the Registry's refusal grounds in the electronic notification; (2) immediately file an amended denomination via the same portal at no additional cost, preserving a new priority date; (3) if the refusal is deemed erroneous, file a 'recurso de alzada' (administrative appeal) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within 1 (one) month from notification, under Articles 121–122 of Law 39/2015; (4) alternatively or subsequently, bring a 'recurso contencioso-administrativo' before the Audiencia Nacional within 2 (two) months; (5) practical SOP: pre-clear the top three alternative names before starting the notarial deed, and execute the public deed immediately upon receipt of the certificate to avoid expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered-address-only virtual offices are tolerated during the pre-incorporation and license-application phase at select Madrid or Barcelona business centers. However, the ISIC 2819 scope (manufacture of high-power fiber laser metal sheet cutting systems) requires a substantive physical footprint: assembly or technical showroom space, warehouse, administrative office with operational staff, municipal building and activity permit (licencia de actividad / apertura), and enrollment in the economic-activity census (IAE). A pure virtual office exposes the company to (i) tax-residence displacement challenges under Article 8 of Law 58/2003, (ii) VAT-registration refusal at the Agencia Tributaria, (iii) AML re-rating above the Low_Risk_Standard tier, and (iv) loss of operational capacity for warranty, spare-parts, and LATAM export logistics.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-Low — approximately 15-25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of activity, driven by Agencia Tributaria controls (Law 58/2003 Articles 142–146), municipal activity-license verification, labor inspectorate visits (Inspección de Trabajo), and possible SEPBLAC-customs co-inspections on imported industrial laser systems; a properly licensed, staffed, and insured facility materially reduces such risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application fee for negative company name certificate (Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social) — standard processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff (Tasa Registral Mercantil — statutory scale; expedited processing surcharge optional)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 20-24, 30-35, 38-40, 43, 93, 159, 210 and 233-234. The minimum capital rule is governed by Article 4 as amended by Law 18/2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent registry is the Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, under the supervision of the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública), Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by an application for registration with the relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Until the capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be transferred to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital upon liquidation if company assets are insufficient. A statutory escrow account is not mandatory; capital may be paid into a company bank account or contributed in kind, subject to deed certification and applicable valuation rules. The amount stated in the deed must be fully subscribed and paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The directors resolve that: (1) the share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] fully paid shares of EUR [nominal value] each, is subscribed by the shareholders in the proportions stated in the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office is adopted at [full address], Spain; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or [names] are appointed as joint or several directors, as specified in the bylaws and deed; (4) the appointed directors are authorized to obtain the company NIF, open and operate bank accounts, execute tax and employment registrations, and complete all filings before the notary, Mercantile Registry, tax authorities, and other competent bodies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-clearance service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and obtain the negative certificate of company name (certificación negativa de denominación social). The certificate is generally reserved for three months for execution of the deed and may be renewed for the statutory registration period. Use the exact approved name in all incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Up to five proposed company names
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or amend the proposed name to remove similarity, prohibited terms, or misleading references. Refile before the certificate expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain foreign shareholder and director identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and designated Spanish diplomatic or tax-administration channels
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-Spanish individual director or shareholder and an NIF for each foreign corporate shareholder. Authenticate foreign corporate documents by apostille or legalization and provide a sworn Spanish translation where required. Prepare beneficial-owner information and powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate certificate of incorporation and good standing, if applicable
Corporate authorization and power of attorney
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure identity or legalization deficiencies by submitting corrected forms, certified copies, translations, or additional evidence requested by the Tax Agency or consular authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed and pay capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario público) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the approved name certificate, bylaws, shareholder details, registered-office evidence, management structure, capital allocation, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the subscribed capital into a company formation bank account when used, or document valid contributions in kind. The notary verifies capacity, powers, legality, and the deed contents, then executes the public deed.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit, if applicable
Registered-office title, lease, or owner authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the notary's qualification request by correcting the bylaws, identification, capital evidence, powers, or foreign-document formalities and execute a rectifying deed if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorized electronic or paper copy of the incorporation deed, together with the required registration forms and tax identification information. The notary may transmit the deed electronically. Monitor the registry entry and obtain the certified registration evidence. Registration gives the company full legal effectiveness as an incorporated entity under the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Powers of attorney, if the filing is not made by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect notice, obtain the written qualification, cure the defects by supplementary or rectifying deed, and resubmit within the applicable correction period. An appeal may be filed with the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, beneficial-owner, and operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, Provincial Mercantile Registry, Social Security Treasury, and competent Autonomous Community and municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the definitive company NIF, register the commencement of business through the census declaration, select the appropriate CNAE activity codes, register directors and employees with Social Security, maintain the beneficial-owner information, and file any required municipal activity, opening, environmental, industrial-establishment, or workplace notifications before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Registered incorporation deed and registry certificate
Technical project and responsible declarations, where required
Environmental, waste, fire, and industrial documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a tax or Social Security query, submit corrected declarations and supporting evidence. For municipal or regional defects, cure the technical deficiency, obtain a revised certificate or project, and refile before commencing the affected activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent authority is the industrial department of the Autonomous Community in which the facility is located, together with the relevant municipality. Spain has no single national manufacturing-licensing board for this activity. The establishment may require registration or notification in the applicable Integrated Industrial Registry under Royal Decree 559/2010 and regional implementing rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal declaración responsable de inicio o apertura or municipal opening/activity licence, as determined by the municipality and Autonomous Community; where classified as an industrial activity, a regional declaración responsable de puesta en servicio de establecimiento industrial or equivalent industrial-establishment registration may also be required. A general national manufacturing permit is not required solely for manufacturing fiber-laser cutting machines.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority is the environmental department of the relevant Autonomous Community; the national framework is administered by the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from formal project-level EIA under Law 21/2013 unless the facility or associated infrastructure falls within Annex I or Annex II thresholds or is subject to cumulative-impact screening. Municipal environmental communication, environmental licence, or integrated environmental authorization may still be required under regional and local law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain sewer or water-discharge authorization where required and comply with applicable regional and municipal effluent limits. Apply Law 34/2007 and Royal Decree 100/2011 for atmospheric emissions, and Royal Decree 117/2003 for VOC emissions when solvent use triggers its thresholds. Manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste under Law 7/2022 and Royal Decree 553/2020, maintain authorized waste-manager records, and comply with applicable noise, refrigerant, oil, packaging, and chemical-storage requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, obtain the applicable municipal fire-safety and emergency-plan clearance and comply with the Basic Fire Safety Regulation in Industrial Establishments under Royal Decree 2267/2004, the Building Code, and applicable municipal rules. Commission structural and floor-load verification for heavy machinery, anchoring, lifting equipment, compressed gases, and storage racks. Implement occupational risk prevention under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 39/1997, including machinery guarding, laser radiation controls, electrical safety, ventilation, training, emergency procedures, and workplace risk assessment. Fiber-laser equipment placed on the EU market must satisfy applicable CE-marking requirements, including the Machinery Directive or Machinery Regulation transition rules, EMC, Low Voltage, and laser-safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Spanish SL, apply for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT using Form 036/037 prior to notarizing the incorporation documents. After registration in the Registro Mercantil and notarial deed filing, AEAT issues the definitive NIF, which also functions as the Spanish VAT identification number. Foreign shareholders holding shares in the SL must obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-N) or, if resident in the EU, have their own EU TIN; the company itself is registered for VAT through the same Form 036, and for intra-Community trade an INTRACOM status and VIES registration are mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box classification. Relevant statutory elections include: group consolidated income tax regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal) for groups with 80% or greater shareholding; the newly established entity reduced corporate rate option; patent royalty regime (notably the patent box); CFC attribution and anti-hybrid mismatch elections under ATAD directives; and special reduced-rate or exempting elections applicable to qualifying financing transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold for Spanish-established companies; any regular taxable activity mandates VAT registration from inception. For EU distance selling, the cross-border registration threshold is €10,000 per calendar year aggregated across EU Member States; non-resident businesses have no threshold and must register from their first taxable supply in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for B2G transactions via Facturae format. Large taxpayers (annual turnover exceeding €6 million) must file real-time VAT information under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) system, submitting invoice records to AEAT within 4 days. From 2025 onward, the Verifactu system will require all B2B electronic invoices to be generated, certified, and transmitted through AEAT-compatible software, with digital stamping and QR-code validation; the system requires API connectivity for real-time fiscal clearance and a non-corruption certificate for the invoicing software.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to third countries outside the EU are exempt from VAT at a 0% effective rate under Ley 37/1992 (Art. 21), provided that the economic ownership of the goods was transferred to the buyer, the goods physically leave EU customs territory, and the export is evidenced by a validated customs declaration. Offshore services provided to B2B customers outside Spain/EU are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT or reverse-charged; they do not benefit from a 0% VAT rate. For goods exports, delivery terms (e.g., FOB, CIF), transport documentation and export licenses must match the contract terms.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUE / SAD) duly accepted and validated by Spanish customs authorities
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill or CMR log evidencing physical dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice and packing list at company letterhead
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT PDF evidencing foreign currency payment receipt and repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT verifies the physical export timeline, transport route, and foreign exchange repatriation. If the export zero-rating is claimed without full documentary substantiation or if foreign currency proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days of shipment/invoice date (unless legally excused), the export is reclassified as domestic supply, leading to assessment of Spanish VAT at 21% on the transaction value, default interest, penalties up to 150% of the VAT amount, and possible additional surcharges for undue refunds. In cases of intentional falsification or fraudulent schemes, serious criminal tax-fraud charges can be brought, and the limitation period for assessment and clawback is 4 years, extendable to 5 years if fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under full capital and current account convertibility as an EU member state. Capital account transactions, including equity injections and intercompany loans, face no quantitative restrictions. Current account items such as trade settlements and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely convertible. Profit repatriation is permitted without FX surrender obligations, subject only to corporate tax filing, beneficial ownership verification, and CRS/FATCA reporting. Hurdles include potential 19% dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders and anti-avoidance rules under EU directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies to export receipts under Spanish law. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted at market rates. All export transactions must be supported by commercial invoices, packing lists, and statistical declarations submitted to Banco de España for balance-of-payments reporting. Conversion is permitted immediately upon receipt with no statutory timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Digital EMIs via licensed Spanish fintechs or EU-regulated platforms (e.g., equivalent to Wise Business) are feasible for operational treasury with full KYC/AML compliance. Offshore digital wallet constraints remain under MiCA and Spanish AMLD5/6 transposition; cross-border remittances require correspondent banking verification and may trigger enhanced due diligence for non-EU destinations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for Spanish SL entities using qualified electronic signatures and video KYC. Physical presence is not mandatory for standard account opening but may be required for initial capital injections exceeding €100,000 or high-value transactions; directors may appoint proxies with notarized power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening adverse hit on directors or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized declarations of clean background, source-of-wealth certificates, and independent verification reports from accredited databases

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure lacking transparency or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registro Mercantil extract, shareholder agreements, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, and legal opinion confirming non-shell status

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source of funds for capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, tax returns, and third-party audit confirmation linking funds to legitimate corporate or personal origins

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires board resolution, beneficial ownership certificate, and proof of equity contribution. Non-resident contributions processed through correspondent banks with full KYC documentation and tax withholding at source where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements executed via SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. Payments routed through correspondent banking networks with proper purpose codes ('PAY' or 'TRADE') and supporting documentation including commercial invoices and shipping documents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting; meeting must be held within 6 months of fiscal year-end (for 31 Dec year-end: filing by 30 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,200 per year; suspension of filing of other corporate documents; after 3 consecutive years of non-filing, the company may be administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 July and 25 July following the fiscal year end (for calendar year end, 31 Dec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 15% of tax due plus daily interest (5%/year); potential tax-inspection penalties of up to 150% of the deficiency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if at least two of the following are met in the two preceding consecutive years: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average employees > 50. Non-listed small/medium entities are exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007); consolidated groups report under IFRS as adopted by EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose an annual UBO confirmation. The UBO register is updated within 7-15 days of any shareholding transfer. The company must maintain a register of members (Libro Registro de Socios) recording all transfers, and changes exceeding the UBO threshold (25%) must be communicated to the Registro de Titularidades Reales.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created eligible entities during the first two taxable periods with positive tax base; R&D and technological innovation tax credits; Patent Box 60% reduction on qualifying income from certain intangibles; free amortisation and enhanced depreciation for qualifying investments. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, subject to offsetting limits of up to 70% of taxable income depending on turnover.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) via the electronic Sede Electrónica portal of the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); mandatory electronic filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following six months after the reporting period's end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF), legal name, tax residence, accounting standard used, and closing date of the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities holding a Spanish permanent establishment (PE) must report the PE-specific NIF and designate a Spanish tax representative if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial result from the profit and loss account before corporate income tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only accounting profits attributable to the Spanish PE using Spanish generally accepted accounting principles or the applicable IFRS framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after permanent and temporary differences, compensation of prior negative tax bases, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure transfer pricing documentation supports any intercompany pricing affecting the Spanish PE; apply arm's length principles before finalising the tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability at the statutory rate before tax credits and reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply applicable treaty rate or domestic non-resident tax rate where a treaty shields PE profits, and document any claimed relief with tax residence certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic corporate income tax credits, double-taxation relief, R&D credits, and Patent Box reductions exercised within statutory limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may only claim credits expressly recognised for Spanish PE activity; attach all supporting documentation for R&D and innovation expenditure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net payable tax after withholdings and prepayments, or amount to be refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile quarterly advance payments already made through Model 202 and ensure settlement matches final liability; late payment interest applies to any under-deposit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without payment triggers a surcharge of 5%–20% depending on delay and statutory late interest. Unjustified late filing where no tax is due incurs fixed penalties from €200 to €1,500. Failure to file within 12 months may generate formal assessment and penalties under Article 191 LGT of 50%–150% of the resulting tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or exempt withholding rate under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by the relevant treaty jurisdiction to the Spanish payer before the payment date. If tax is withheld at source, the recipient may file Form 210 for refund through the AEAT within the statute of limitations period, attaching the TRC and evidence of beneficial ownership. For EU/EEA-related dividends, the parent-subsidiary directive may apply when the holding threshold and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate is 19% on royalty payments for patents, trademarks, know-how, and similar IP, and 19% on cross-border debt interest. Under EU Interest and Royalties Directive, related-company payments meeting the 25% holding or qualifying control conditions may be exempt. Tax treaties commonly reduce rates to 0%–15% depending on the applicable treaty and beneficiary structure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory for taxpayers with annual net turnover exceeding €10,000,000; Master File required when consolidated group turnover exceeds €45,000,000. Lower thresholds may apply in certain high-risk or tax-haven transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but general anti-abuse principles, the substance-over-form doctrine (Article 15 LGT), the anti-fragmentation and entity re-characterisation rules (Article 15 LIS), and CFC rules (Article 100 LIS) impose de facto substance requirements. A Spanish SL must demonstrate real personnel, premises, decision-making, and economic activity to avoid re-characterisation and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting taxable income derived from exports or domestic sales, inflating deductions, or omitting income from a Spanish permanent establishment when manufacturing and selling fiber laser cutting machines in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Article 305 Penal Code when defrauded amount exceeds €120,000: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years, fine of 1 to 6 times the defrauded amount, loss of grants or public benefits. Legal entities face fines up to €1,100,000 and possible suspension or dissolution under Article 310bis Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the civil tax debt under Article 42 Ley General Tributaria and, in cases of criminal evasion, face personal imprisonment, travel bans, forfeiture of assets, and restitution obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or operating an SL without real employees, physical premises, inventory, or manufacturing activity, used purely as an invoicing or profit-repatriation conduit for the laser-cutting equipment sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities can re-characterise the simulated entity under Article 15 LGT, disregard its separate personality, and recalculate tax as if the transaction had been conducted by the underlying principal. Adjustments attract late interest plus penalties under Article 191 LGT up to 150% of the underpaid tax, and the entity may be denied treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced; directors incur personal responsibility for the full unpaid amount, civil restitution, possible restriction on managing Spanish companies, and if fraud is proven, imprisonment under Article 305 Penal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling high-power fiber laser cutting machines to a related-party distributor at below-arm's-length margins or entering into arrangements intended to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions without preparing Local File or Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish tax authorities may apply the arm's-length standard and impose a penalty of 15% of the resulting valuation adjustment under Article 271.5 LGT, plus late interest. Failure to provide requested documentation triggers separate penalties from €1,500 to €15,000 per item, and incorrect documentation may lead to additional fines under Article 198 LGT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be considered jointly liable for the corrected corporate tax debt and penalty, and may be subject to disqualification orders if intentional concealment is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting SWIFT LC or TT Wire payments from transaction parties in FATF high-risk jurisdictions without conducting adequate beneficial-ownership and money-laundering due diligence, or using unverified shell company intermediaries for the laser machine sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010 on money-laundering prevention, serious infractions carry fines up to €150,000; very serious infractions carry fines from €150,000 to €1,500,000, publication of the sanction, and prohibition on conducting regulated business operations. If the funds derive from underlying crime, criminal money-laundering liability arises under Article 301 Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal monetary penalties, travel restrictions, prohibition from managing financial or industrial entities, and criminal imprisonment in aggravated money-laundering cases.
